chunks: Abu Ali al-Ash'ari, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar, from Ibn Fazzal, from Tha'laba ibn Maymun, from Abu Basir, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
The judgements are two judgements — a Judgement of God and a judgement of ignorance (Jahiliyya).
And indeed God, Mighty and Majestic, has said: And who is better than God to judge for a people who are certain?
And bear witness against Zayd ibn Thabit — indeed he judged in matters of obligatory inheritance according to the judgement of ignorance.

key_terms.الْجَاهِلِيَّةِ: Jahiliyya — the era and culture of pre-Islamic ignorance; by extension, any ruling contrary to divine law
key_terms.الْحُكْمُ: Judgement, legal ruling, authority (hukm) — a comprehensive term for law and governance
key_terms.الْفَرَائِضِ: Al-fara'id — the obligatory inheritance shares defined by Quranic law (also called 'ilm al-fara'id)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam al-Baqir say about the two types of judgement and Zayd ibn Thabit?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (AS) presents a binary framework for all legal rulings: every judgement is either from God or from the pre-Islamic era of ignorance (Jahiliyya). He supports this with a direct Quranic citation (5:50) challenging anyone to claim superiority over God's judgement. Crucially, the Imam then publicly names Zayd ibn Thabit — a companion revered by Sunnis as a leading authority on inheritance law — and declares that his rulings on obligatory inheritance shares deviated from God's law and fell into the category of Jahiliyya judgement. This hadith reflects the Shia legal tradition's sharp critique of certain companion-based jurisprudence and insistence that authentic Islamic law must derive solely from the Quran and the Ahl al-Bayt.

en.hubeali:
Abu Ali Al Ashary, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Jabbar, from Ibn Fazzal, from Sa’alba Bin Maymoun, from Abu Baseer, 
Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> has said:
‘The judgements are two judgements – a Judgement of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> and a judgement of the ignorance,
and Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic has Said [5:50] And who is better than Allah to Judge for a people who are certain?,
and (I<sup>asws</sup>) bear witness that Zayd Bin Sabit had judged with regards to the Obligations by the judgement of the ignorance’.
en.sarwar: 2. Abu Ali al-Ash‘ariy has narrated from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Jabbar from ibn Faddal from Tha‘labah ibn Maymun from abu Basir who has narrated the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Judgments and laws are of two kinds: the judgment of Allah and the judgment of ignorance. Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, has said, “
. . . who is a better judge than Allah for a believing people.” [5:59]

You all must bear testimony that Zayd ibn Thabit issued a judgment in matters of obligations according to the judgment of ignorance.’” (In the case of a contracting slave-girl and her fornication Zayd judged opposite to the judgment of Ali, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, in the time of ‘Uthman)
